summary: The fixable part is done: #710 (60633eff3) added structural directory reconciliation and a no-op patch guard, so a re-read that changes nothing no longer publishes a new nodes array or re-renders anything. The auditor's remaining item, skipping the first-ready invalidation with an #everReady flag, rests on a wrong premise and would cause a regression. The first ready is not redundant. On a cold start the directory read (state.ts:752-753) and the routed thread-cache prefetch are sent beside the session restore. The Hub session socket is only created after the store becomes authenticated (hubSession.ts:63,73-99). The Hub adds the socket to its invalidation fan-out (indexSession) only when the upgrade opens, just before it sends ready. Every cold-start read is therefore answered before this browser is subscribed, and a change in that window reaches the browser only through the ready-time re-read. It is the subscribe-then-read barrier. Removing it would save almost nothing. On the directory side, the cold-start read normally finishes before the socket is online, so it schedules the next poll at the unsubscribed 20 s cadence, and nothing reschedules that poll when the subscription comes online. Skipping the ready re-read would only move the same GET /api/nodes to t+20 s and leave the race open until then. On the thread-cache side, the re-reads already present the held version (If-None-Match, so 304/null in the common case). While the subscription is online there is no time-based shell or thread refresh, so dropping the barrier could leave a node's cached shell stale until some other thread-cache invalidation arrives. The existing test (hostedHubSession.test.ts:145-161) and docs/hub-session-protocol.md:54 treat the ready invalidation as intended. Nothing valid remains for this finding.

evidence.note: Still calls #notifyInvalidation({directory:true, threadCache:true}) on every ready, the first one included. This is unchanged and serves as the barrier (see below), not waste.

#restoreAccess sends restoreSession and #prefetchDirectory together (752-753). The prefetched directory is committed at 773, after the authenticated patch at 765. #resumeBrowser does the same at 2055-2072. The directory read leaves before any Hub session socket exists.

sync() creates and starts the HostedHubSession only once accountStatus is authenticated (63, 73-99), which is after the cold-start directory and thread-cache prefetch reads were sent. onInvalidate at 84-88 forwards to notifyDirectoryInvalidated and to the listeners.

origin/main: the open handler calls indexSession(socket) (471) and then sends ready (473). The fan-out at 278-307 reaches only sockets in sessions/sessionsByScope, so a change made after the Hub answered a cold-start read but before indexSession is never pushed to this browser. The ready-time re-read is the only thing that closes that gap.

The poll is scheduled at DIRECTORY_SUBSCRIBED_REFRESH_MS (120 s) only if hasLiveHubSubscription() is true when the read completes. Otherwise it is DIRECTORY_REFRESH_MS (20 s, line 488). The only #scheduleDirectory callers are 2223, 2317 and 2352, so nothing reschedules on subscription online. The cold-start read usually finishes before ready, so skipping the ready re-read would only move the GET /api/nodes to t+20 s, not remove it.

With the subscription online, shells are refreshed only when nextShellRefresh === 0 (484-488), and the 15 s interval re-reads the thread only when !isSubscriptionOnline (521-524). Invalidations are the only refresh trigger while subscribed, so the ready invalidation (514-519) is the thread cache's only barrier against reads answered before the subscription existed. The prefetch at 332-397 is sent beside the access check.

The barrier re-reads are conditional: readShell gets shells.get(node.id) as held, and readThread gets details...get(threadId) at 294. api.ts:2451/2468 sends If-None-Match. The thread-cache part of the cost is therefore N+1 cheap not-modified round trips, not full bodies.

listNodes has no If-None-Match, so the barrier directory re-read (like every poll) returns a full body of a few KB at most 16 nodes. That is the only non-trivial residual cost, and it is not specific to this finding.

Fixed part from 60633eff3 (#710). reconcileDirectoryNodes keeps unchanged node objects and returns the previous array when nothing changed. The guard at 2306-2315 publishes no patch when every key is Object.is-equal, and refreshedSelection reuses the selected object (2277-2280). Its doc comment (423-428) names 'the reconnect re-read' as a case it makes cheap, so the authors deliberately kept the barrier and made it cheap.

The test expects onInvalidate twice (161), from the first ready plus one explicit invalidate, so first-ready invalidation is pinned as intended behaviour. docs/hub-session-protocol.md:54 also documents that reconnection invalidates both domains.

fixDefects: None found in the implemented part. reconcileDirectoryNodes handles reordering by id, keeps per-node identity, and returns the previous array when nothing changed. The patch guard compares every key with Object.is. The auditor's own closing change (an #everReady flag that skips the first ready) would itself be a defect if implemented, for the reasons in the summary.
implementationSketch: No change for this finding. Do NOT add an #everReady flag or a reconnect-only invalidation in packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.ts. The first ready is the barrier for reads the Hub answered before indexSession, and a client-side 'read started after connect began' heuristic cannot prove ordering against the Hub's indexSession either. A correct reduction would need either (a) a Hub-side ETag/If-None-Match on GET /api/nodes so the barrier re-read and the 120 s polls become 304s (Hub API change plus listNodes in packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:2474 passing the held tag), or (b) domain revisions in the ready frame (Hub protocol change). Both are general optimisations outside this finding and low value (one body of a few KB per connect). Optionally, a small test in threadReadCache.test.ts or state.test.ts could pin that a ready-time invalidation after a read sent before the subscription triggers exactly one conditional re-read, so a future 'optimisation' does not silently remove the barrier.
decisionReason: Nothing to implement. The optional ETag or ready-revision alternatives would be Hub API or protocol changes needing a Hub deploy, and would need their own decision if anyone pursued them.
